reviews.title: Premium Ultra Paywalls Broken Features (Dev Knows & Won't Fix)
reviews.text:
Do not pay for the top-tier "Premium Ultra" subscription if you are buying it for automated Live Activities or background precipitation alerts.
The entire selling point of the top subscription tier is turnkey, automated Live Activities that are supposed to initiate on your Lock Screen and Dynamic Island before it rains and continuously update in the background. In reality, it does neither. The Live Activity fails to auto-start, and once forced open manually, it freezes and refuses to refresh in the background unless you constantly babysit and open the app.
When contacted with technical documentation, the developer acknowledged server-side and platform token drop failures in their push-to-start system. Instead of fixing the broken feature or updating the marketing copy, the developer dismissed it as a standard "bug" and instructed me to request a refund through Apple.
Charging a steep, recurring subscription premium while knowing the underlying background infrastructure does not reliably work is deceptive. Save your money—the basic tiers or free weather apps work just as well without paying extra for broken features.

reviews.title: Disappointing Accuracy — Not Worth the Price
reviews.text:
I really wanted to like CARROT Weather. I’ve been using it since August, hoping it would live up to the reputation of being a better alternative to Dark Sky. Unfortunately, my experience has been the opposite.

The biggest problem is the hyper-local precipitation alerts. In my experience, they are wrong roughly 95% of the time. Just yesterday, I received an alert saying rain would begin in about five minutes. I immediately opened CARROT’s radar to see what was approaching—and there was no rain showing anywhere within roughly 50 miles of my location. That’s not a minor miss; it makes the alert essentially useless.

The regular forecasts have also been disappointing. Temperatures are frequently off by several degrees, and I’ve had numerous occasions where rain was forecast but never materialized in my area. For a weather app that emphasizes detailed and accurate forecasting, I expected considerably better performance.

The other issue is the price. CARROT offers a lot of features, but I have a hard time justifying the subscription cost when the most important thing I need from a weather app—the actual weather forecast and precipitation alerts—isn’t consistently accurate.

I was hoping CARROT would give me the experience I loved with Dark Sky. Instead, after several months of use, I find myself getting results that are not noticeably better than Apple Weather, which now incorporates technology from Dark Sky.

reviews.title: Trim and focus and make it cheaper
reviews.text:
I literally just did a review then an app update came through stripping even more features!

I’ve had this now for a couple of years, pay the price as it makes me smile. I pay £19.49 a year, now, for the weather, something readily available for free from lots of places, so that’s a lot!
I’ve watched the app get stuffed with unnecessary features, get messy, and slowly things getting stripped away for ‘ultra’ even basic things or just handy things like Apple car play. Now that the edge of the comedy aspect and pretty graphics is wearing off this is beginning to really annoy me, the weather accuracy has also gotten worse and having just done the app update you’ve stripped away multi day on the sonar, what next! I mean, come on. 
So, I’ll give it 6 months, I hope you’re the type of developers that look at reviews and take on board the criticism from your loyal customers … whether you act on it is your choice, but I will be cancelling and deleting if things don’t improve.

reviews.text:
I’d love to say it’s worth the price and there’s no doubt the app goes an extra mile but the problem is that it’s a one-trick pony that (on the “free” version spends more time bugging you to buy the upgrade than it does proving useful information. 

It does smell more strongly of AI now than I remember;  I’ve been dropping in and out since the early days.

So yeah, still great fun, but that doesn’t come close to justifying the price or the adverts to buy it. 

And since licensing is clearly a “moving target” these days, I refuse to take anything anyone says up front.

reviews.title: AI Drivel Ruined Carrot
reviews.text: I was truly a super fan of Carrot, all of my conversations that pertained to weather were accented by an enthusiastic shoutout to this once creative app. That changed suddenly when I opened the app for my daily dose of snark and information to be met with.. AI background music? l get the gag is that Carrot is a “snarky robot”, but the human creativity that drove this app was the entire point. It made the mundane chore of evaluating daily weather patterns into something fun and unique, and because humans were writing the lines, it felt like you were hearing about news/weather patterns from a sarcastic friend. The AI music is uninspired, and takes up too much of the UI to even think about keeping the app. The sudden shift to AI explains the uninspired dialogue and subscription price hikes as of late (which I didn’t even attribute to AI until the awful music, perhaps a blessing in disguise). The data isn’t even comprehensive without a subscription, pursue another weather app - this one is extremely disappointing.
